solutionSql:
SELECT shipment_id, event_id, status, occurred_at
FROM (
  SELECT shipment_id,
         id AS event_id,
         status,
         occurred_at,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
           PARTITION BY shipment_id
           ORDER BY occurred_at DESC, id DESC
         ) AS rn
  FROM shipment_events
) ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY shipment_id;

rules.howSolved: Used ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by shipment_id over shipment_events and kept rn = 1, so each shipment with events gets one row and shipments without events never appear.
Ordered the window by occurred_at DESC as the first key.
Ordered the window by id DESC as the second key, so the greatest event id wins a timestamp tie.

notes: Timestamps are timestamptz, so comparison is by absolute instant. Ties on (shipment_id, occurred_at) occur in several datasets and are resolved by id. Row counts per dataset: sample=218, nulls=109, ties=163, boundary=163. Ran on every listed dataset without error.
